subject: MSA + Order Form: safeguard language, service-of-process, and notice flow
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@gatewayai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procure@gatewayai.com, Alex Tan <alex.tan@gatewayai.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Gateway redlines for Redwood MSA (initial pass)

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Attached is Gateway's initial redline pass on the MSA and a short note on the Order Form. Our main asks on the dispute/disclaimer sections are:

- Governing law: prefer State of New York for commercial predictability; consider split venue for injunctive relief.
- Injunctive relief: Gateway needs an explicit carve that permits equitable relief in courts where our assets reside (we operate globally).
- Arbitration: we can agree to arbitration for monetary claims, but want a carveout for emergency injunctive relief and preservation orders.
- Service of process / consent to personal jurisdiction: we want to avoid open-ended consent that could be used for unexpected waivers.

We attached a redline (Gateway_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx) and a marked-up Order Form (Gateway_OrderForm_Annotated.pdf). Can you confirm internal review timeline? Procurement is aiming to finalize before the end of the quarter.

Thanks,

Maria Gomez
General Counsel, Gateway AI
maria.gomez@gatewayai.com

Attachment: Gateway_MSA_Redlines_v2.docx (Word document, 73 KB)
Attachment: Gateway_OrderForm_Annotated.pdf (PDF, 48 KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@gatewayai.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 7 Apr 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway redlines for Redwood MSA (initial pass)

Maria —

Appreciate the quick redline. Looping in Karthish (legal) and Kimberly (GC) to weigh in on the specific carve language. High-level thoughts before they review:

- We are open to NY governing law for the MSA, but prefer to keep service/consent language narrow to avoid broad personal jurisdiction waivers.
- Carveout for injunctive/emergency relief is reasonable; we typically include a limited "break-glass" that allows either party to seek provisional relief in court for preservation and confidentiality. We'll want to align on venue scope for that carve.
- For arbitration, our standard is that monetary claims go to arbitration, and injunctive relief is carved out — which sounds aligned. We need to ensure the Order Form's acceptance of the model / infra SLAs doesn't create separate dispute paths.

Karthik / Kimberly — can you review the attached Gateway redlines and propose a compromise clause (governing-law + provisional relief + service-of-process) that we can send back as a single tracked-change file? Procurement would like next-gen language to present to their execs on Friday (4/10).

Logan
Account Executive — Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: maria.gomez@gatewayai.com
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway redlines for Redwood MSA (initial pass) — proposed compromise

Logan / Kimberly —

Thanks, Logan. I reviewed Gateway's redlines and drafted a compromise that minimizes downstream risk while addressing Gateway's operational concerns. Key points (high level):

1) Governing law: Accept New York law for the MSA but add a clause that the Order Form's enforcement of emergency relief can be sought in a court where the party has substantial assets or where injunctive relief is immediately available. Wording proposed: "Notwithstanding the governing law selection, either party may seek injunctive or other provisional relief in any competent court with jurisdiction over such relief to preserve rights, property, or confidential information."

2) Arbitration carveout: Keep monetary disputes to arbitration (per our standard clause). Explicitly carve emergency provisional relief and preservation measures out of arbitration. Add a 14-day notice-and-cure window for non-emergency injunctive requests to encourage dialogue, but make clear that the window does not apply to immediate preservation steps.

3) Service of process / consent: Narrow the consent language — consent to service of process only for enforcement of a final arbitration award or for actions seeking injunctive relief under the carveout. Do not consent to general long-arm jurisdiction beyond what is reasonably necessary.

4) Order Form coupling: Add a short cross-reference in the Order Form noting that venue exceptions and provisional relief carveouts in the MSA apply to any Order Form disputes. This prevents conflicting paths.

I've attached a tracked file "MSA_fallback_proposal_k.iyer.docx" with exact language. If Gateway accepts that form of compromise, we can produce a clean redline for signature.

Recommended next steps:
- Logan to share the attached proposal with Gateway and ask for confirmation on the 14-day non-emergency notice.
- If they accept, we prepare the final signature-ready MSA + updated Order Form.

Kimberly, if you see anything that needs tightening (consent scope, forum selection phrasing) please flag.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: MSA_fallback_proposal_k.iyer.docx (Word, 12 KB)

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@gatewayai.com>

Cc: alice.procure@gatewayai.com, Alex Tan <alex.tan@gatewayai.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2026 08:49:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway redlines for Redwood MSA (initial pass) — acceptance + clarification

Logan / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. Gateway is generally comfortable with the compromise as written. A couple of clarifying points before we sign:

- The 14-day notice period is acceptable for non-emergency injunctive requests. We acknowledge the carveout for immediate preservation.
- On venue: we want to ensure that seeking emergency relief in a non-NY court won’t be interpreted as waiving Gateway's right to object to jurisdiction for other claims. Can you add a one-sentence confirmation that seeking provisional relief in a local court will not be construed as consent to general jurisdiction except to the extent necessary to enforce the provisional relief?

We have a DocuSign packet ready for the most recent clean Order Form + MSA once you provide the final tracked changes. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/r/EXAMPLE-239023 (Gateway packet)

We'd prefer to get a final countersigned MSA this week — procurement has internal deadlines.

Best,

Maria Gomez
General Counsel, Gateway AI

Quoted: "MSA_fallback_proposal_k.iyer.docx attached""

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway redlines for Redwood MSA (initial pass) — final tweaks and go/no-go

All —

Thanks, everyone. I reviewed the proposal and Maria's clarification request. I'm comfortable with the compromise but made two very small edits in the proposed language to close potential interpretation gaps:

- Added explicit sentence: "Pursuit of provisional relief under this Section shall not constitute a waiver of any party's right to contest personal jurisdiction or venue for any claims not related to such provisional relief, except to the limited extent necessary to effectuate such provisional relief."
- Clarified that the 14-day notice-and-cure applies only to non-emergency injunctive measures and cannot be used to delay preservation steps (example language included in attachment).

I'll produce a final tracked-change clean copy and upload to the HubSpot deal. Logan — please share the DocuSign link with our sales ops team and coordinate final signature. Once countersigned, hand off to CS for onboarding and include the venue carve notes in the implementation runbook.

Kimberly Park
General Counsel (Acting)
Redwood Inference
